f8e833b3b9.q: What was the scale and cost of the British military expedition to rescue hostages from Emperor Teodros II in Abyssinia?
f8e833b3b9.a: The expedition cost the British taxpayer 10 million pounds, equivalent to tens of billions of pounds in today's money. Napier planned the campaign methodically, requiring 5,000 men to extract hostages, another 10,000 to guard supply lines, and drawing on resources across the entire British Empire including 13,000 soldiers, 20 miles of railway track, and 44 elephants shipped across the Indian Ocean by January 1868.

a43989c024.q: How did Lieutenant General Robert Napier use diplomacy to secure local support for the Abyssinian expedition?
a43989c024.a: Napier stopped in the territory of Kassa, the king of Tigray, and greeted him with full military honors. He presented gifts including an Arabian horse, a rifle, and glassware, and promised that his troops would not loot or steal, paying for every sack of grain. In return, Kassa gave him a lion's skin cloak and weekly supplies of food, with an implicit understanding that Napier would deal with Teodros once and for all.

d16fd8b481.q: What currency did British forces use to conduct transactions in East Africa during the 1868 Abyssinian campaign?
d16fd8b481.a: British agents discovered that the only commonly accepted universal currency in East Africa was the Austrian silver tala, first minted by Maria Theresa in 1741. The 1780 edition was particularly valued. Napier sent representatives to the official mint in Vienna, which agreed to produce 20,000 of these coins per week purely for the expeditionary force.

bb3778c9c0.q: What technological innovations did Napier incorporate into the Abyssinian expedition to maintain control and logistics?
bb3778c9c0.a: Napier brought seven photographers, a portable telegraph system, water pumps, flares to light up camp at night, and copper telegraph wire. His sappers unspooled copper wire all the way to their advance guard as they progressed. The campaign was described as the most technologically advanced military campaign in history, including 20 miles of railway track, pile driving machinery, and hundreds of tons of coal.

abbc843455.q: Why was the Austrian Maria Theresa silver coin still used as currency in East Africa in the 1950s?
abbc843455.a: The reason why these coins became entrenched and accepted in East Africa remains undetermined. The coins had simply become so accepted as a standard that they persisted as currency long after their original circulation period, remaining in use in the 1950s despite no longer being minted in Vienna.

04f962784b.q: What were the challenges facing British military planners in launching an intervention against Emperor Teodros in Abyssinia?
04f962784b.a: Intelligence was absolutely useless with the Abyssinian interior not properly mapped and consisting of challenging mountains. British officers in Bombay concluded that 'there are few countries about which we know less.'
